original: 二九日 一五一五 N一七-一三 E一一八-二二 みりい丸 さらわく丸 (小破)
translation: 29th, 1515, N 17°13′ E 118°22′: Miri Maru and Sarawak Maru (minor damage)
note: 1st Surface Escort Division war diary, June 1944, chart 別表第二 船団護衛状況(馬来直航路) (convoy escort, Malay direct route): handwritten beside a torpedo symbol on convoy ヒ67 (HI-67)'s track, which ends at (マニラ) Manila. Written in Arabic numerals in the original (290 1515 / N17-13 / E118-22)

original: (ハ) 小破 有馬山丸、神州丸、みりい丸、さらわく丸、まりふ丸 中破 能登呂
translation: (c) Minor damage: Arimasan Maru, Shinshu Maru, Miri Maru, Sarawak Maru, Marifu Maru. Moderate damage: Notoro
note: Same diary, notes to table 別表第一 (escort statistics, June). Neither oiler is in the June list of ships sunk by submarine (9 ships, 43,073 tons with one lost to aircraft). Notoro's damage was FLASHER's, off Borneo at about 0117 the same day (combinedfleet.com Notoro_t), not BANG's; Marifu Maru's was FLIER's on 13 June

translation: BANG fires all ten tubes at three ships at about 1510; Sarawak Maru is hit in the bow and Miri Maru under the bridge, and both reach Manila
note: Secondary. Time "about 1510" is BANG's (sheet 1508-1509 I); position is the source's. Temporary repairs at Cavite until 24 July
